newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Greenpeace alleges shots fired in Portugal protest.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace alleges shots fired in Portugal protest.

text.p: Environmental group Greenpeace said on Thursday it would protest to the Portuguese government after police fired shots when activists tried to block a ship carrying gene-modified maize from entering a Lisbon harbour.

"Police on a patrol boat using automatic weapons fired shots over our heads when we tried to prevent the Pacificator from docking around one a.m. (0100 gmt)," campaign coordinator Ricardo Aguilar told Reuters. No one was hit, he said.

"When we saw that their action was aggressive, we decided to cancel the protest. We were carrying some independent journalists on the inflatables and we didn't want them to get hurt. Ours was a peaceful protest," he added.

The Cypriot-owned Pacificator, which transported genetically modified maize from Louisiana, docked on Thursday morning at Lisbon harbour and unloaded 14,500 tonnes of maize, probably intended for use as cattle fodder, local media said.
"Greenpeace International will be making a formal complaint about excessive use of force to the Portuguese authorities," the group said in a statement issued in Amsterdam.
The alleged shooting incident occurred during the second attempt of the Greenpeace protesters to prevent the docking.
On Wednesday afternoon, five protesters chained themselves to the harbour wall and colleagues in four motorised dinghies harassed the ship until the evening low tide prevented it from docking.

Aguilar echoed concern among Western environmentalists that genetic alterations could lead to an increase in the resistance of bacteria to antibiotics and could encourage insects to become more resistant to pesticide strains.
"Greenpeace is calling on the Portuguese government to ban the import of the transgenic corn in order to protect Europeans' environment and health," Greenpeace International said.
"In spite of serious concerns regarding possible health and environmental implications, the corn was approved by the European Commission earlier this month," it said.
Protesters had painted the slogan "No X Corn" on the side of the ship, witnesses said. "X" means genetically-engineered, Aguilar said.
